# Barrett WAM's PyBullet and Pinocchio End-Effector Position Match but Velocity Discrepancy, What Was Verified in the Original Thread?

> **Current answer:** The original thread validated alignment of the reference frame (ReferenceFrame): the responder suggested changing Pinocchio's velocity/Jacobian to LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED. The original author reported it seems to work, and contributors to the Pinocchio project later acknowledged the answer. The response also explains that WORLD represents spatial velocity in the fixed coordinate system, while LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED aligns the LOCAL body Jacobian with the world direction using the rotation R from the link frame. This can be written as J_lwa = [R, 0; 0, R] * J_local. The original graph only showed position overlap before correction and inconsistent velocities, so it cannot be extrapolated to all simulation differences.

## Effective fixes

- Use LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED to express the end-effector velocity/Jacobian in the original PyBullet comparison.
